first: Dark water, a jetty, and a man with an oar. "First time. Everyone has one. Your things are with me; we'll talk about them when you're on your feet."
The ferryman doesn't look up from the water. "{name}. New face. Sit. The cold stops in a moment."
obol: The ferryman turns something small over in his fingers. "You brought an obol. I noticed. I took it."
"An obol in the pack." He pockets it. "Someone taught you manners. That covers it."
free: The ferryman weighs your pack in one hand and shrugs. "Not worth the argument. You can have it back."
"This?" He holds up what you carried. "I've fished better out of the river."
again: The ferryman is already waiting. "{name}. Back so soon."
"Again." He sets your things on the jetty beside him. "They're safe with me. For a while."
The water is very still. "You know how this goes," says the ferryman.
frequent: "{name}. Death number {deaths}." The ferryman makes room on the bench. "I'm starting to keep your seat warm."
The ferryman has your side of the boat cleared before you arrive. "I took the liberty."
